There is one PSOC located within the 200-foot radius (Zone 1) surrounding, Well 2 and Well 3 (Figure No. 4). The access road [Transportation Road Corridor (PSOC 007)] from Fairview Avenue to the well field is a source of petroleum contaminants including gasoline and diesel fuels, which contain volatile organic compounds. The sedimentary materials present at Well 2 and Well 3 include about 5 feet of silty topsoil atop 30 feet of unconsolidated, permeable sands and gravels overlying low permeability silty clay. The wells obtain groundwater from the well screens positioned in the prolific sand and gravel aquifer at a depth of 25 to 30 feet. There is little protection provided to the unconfined groundwater aquifer from contaminants released to the surface. Therefore, the presence of PSOC 007 within Zone 1 of the three wells requires that it is given a "high" risk rating.

There are four identified PSOC's located within Zone 2 of Well 2 and Well 3 (Figure No. 4). The closest PSOC's are Transportation Road Corridors (PSOC 007) and a sewage pump station (PSOC 010). The roads are located throughout the southern and the western (up gradient) portion of Zone 2. The sewage pump station (PSOC 10) is located at the West Rutland Recreation Building, 225 feet south of Well 3, and 325 feet south of Well 2. Wastewater generated in the building is pumped up into the municipal sewer main on Fairview Avenue. Contaminants associated with PSOC 10 include nitrate, bacteria, viruses and other pathogens. ASTs (PSOC 008) containing fuel oil for interior space heating and hot water generation are located within residential buildings in Zone 2. Contaminants associated with AST's include VOCs. The actual locations of ASTs were not confirmed, but are known to be associated with many of the developed properties, the majority of which are located west of Well 2 and Well 3. Some buildings are provided propane gas for heating and hot water. Propane is not considered a PSOC since it is a gas and if released would be dispersed in the air and would not flow downward through soils and impact groundwater. To the south of the two wells is Agricultural Activity (PSOC 003) occurring on open farmland. Contaminants associated with PSOC 003 include nitrate, bacteria, fertilizers and synthetic organic chemicals (SOC's). Sedimentary materials underlying these developed properties in Zone 2 consist of glacial kame sand and gravel atop glacial till. The sand and gravel are permeable and allow contaminants to migrate vertically downward and flow with shallow groundwater in the subsurface. However, the underlying glacial till atop bedrock is generally denser (a basal till that was overridden by the glacial ice) and of low permeability, thereby retarding or preventing the migration of shallow contaminants into the underlying deeper 115 | P a g e West Rutland Zoning Regulations (Adopted 2022) bedrock aquifer. Due to the presence of PSOC's 003, 007, 008 and 010 within Zone 2 and the lack of low permeability confining sedimentary materials atop the sand and gravel aquifer supplying groundwater to the wells, "high" risk ratings have been assigned to each of these four PSOC's.

Zone 3 is the largest single area within the SPA and lies west, southwest and south of Well 2 and Well 3 (Figure No. 4). Included within Zone 3 are undeveloped and developed properties. Most developed properties consist of residential homes. The undeveloped properties include forested land and open land consisting of meadows and agricultural farmland. Nine PSOC's are located in Zone 3. PSOC's 003, 007 and 008 described previously in Zones 1 and 2 are also present in Zone 3. Agricultural Activity (PSOC 003) occurs to the south of the two wells. Manure is spread on the fields, the SOC herbicide glyphosate is applied to emergent corn, and the fields are fertilized. Best management practices are utilized to avoid excess PSOC applications. Transportation Road Corridors (PSOC 007) are located throughout Zone 3. ASTs containing fuel oil for interior heating and hot water generation are located at some residences and commercial facilities. A junkyard (PSOC 002) was formerly located to the west of wells 2 and 3 at the Casella Waste Management property. The property was cleaned up and is now occupied as a truck repair facility, a recycling facility, and for the storage of empty dumpsters. The Casella Waste Management property is a former Hazardous Material Spill Site (PSOC 004). During excavation and removal of a 6,000 gallon UST containing waste oil in June 1996, soil and groundwater contamination was discovered. As a result, the Sites Management Section (SMS) classified the property as Hazardous Waste Site #96-2024. A contaminant investigation was completed by Heindel & Noyes in 1997, and included the installation of groundwater monitoring wells and the collection of groundwater quality samples. In February 1998, the Vermont Waste Management Division (WMD) issued a site closure letter indicating that the sources of contamination at the site had been adequately characterized and remediated (UST and contaminated soils were removed), the site does not pose an unreasonable risk to human health or the environment, and sampling of groundwater does not show any impacts to groundwater at the site. An existing petroleum UST (PSOC 005) for refueling trucks is located west of Wells 2 and 3 on the Casella Waste Management property. An out-of service gasoline UST and decrepit pump are located at the base of Clark Hill Road, southwest of Wells 2 and 3. Contaminants associated with USTs are VOCs. A small Cemetery (PSOC 006) containing about 20 headstones is located to the southwest of Wells 2 and 3 between North Lane and Westside Court. The cemetery was used in the early 1900's and is no longer in use. The cemetery is surrounded by residences. Contaminants associated with cemeteries include VOCs, SOCs, embalming fluids, arsenic and biological products. A Vehicle Repair Shop (PSOC 009) is located along Clarendon Avenue to the south-southwest of Wells 2 and 3. "Frank and Joe's Auto and Truck Repair" performs 116 | P a g e West Rutland Zoning Regulations (Adopted 2022) mechanical and auto body repairs, and installs spray-on truck bed liners. Contaminants associated with PSOC 009 include VOC's, SOCs, antifreeze, solvents and metals. The Casella Waste Management property west of Wells 2 and 3 also is a Vehicle Repair Shop (PSOC 009) that performs maintenance and repairs on their fleet of trucks. On-site sewage disposal (PSOC 001) occurs on four residential properties located along Dewey Avenue and Clark Hill Road, in the far southwestern portion of Zone 3. Properly designed and maintained septic systems provide sufficient treatment of wastewater prior to the discharged effluent contacting the shallow groundwater system. Contaminants associated with on-site septic systems include nitrate, bacteria, viruses and household cleaners. Sedimentary materials present beneath PSOC's 002, 003, 004, 005, 006, 007, 008 and 009 in Zone 3 include permeable, glacial kame, sand and gravel atop dense glacial till. Sedimentary materials present beneath PSOC 001 in the southwestern portion of Zone 3 are dense, low permeability, glacial till underlain by bedrock. All PSOC's in Zone 3 are given a "low" risk rating due to the generally great distance to Wells 2 and 3. However, since PSOC's 003, 007, 008 and 010 are located within Zone 2; they will remain as "high" risk. PSOC's 001, 002, 004, 005, 006 and 009 are rated as "low" risk in Zone 3. PSOC 009 is given a "moderate" risk rating. Refer to Tables 2 and 3 for the summarized PSOC's and risk ratings.

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Potential for Future Development and Assessmen t of Future Risks
paragraphs: Future land development within the Source Protection Area should be monitored for its potential impact to the West Rutland Fire District No. 1 water supply (Figure No.3). There is no future development potential for SPA Zone 1 since all activities in this area are exclusively reserved for the source wells and water system. Based on the Town of West Rutland Zoning Regulations, adopted June 28, 2004, the future development potential for SPA Zone 2 includes Residential 2 development. Future development land uses in SPA Zone 3 includes Residential 2, Industrial, and Conservation 1 development. The Industrial zone is in the area of the existing Casella Waste Management property to the west of Wells 2 and 3. The Conservation 1 zone is in the uplands to the west-southwest and southwest of Wells 2 and 3 along Dewey Road and Clark Hill Road. Increased residential development will be mitigated by maintenance or upgrades of the community sewer system and public awareness. Physical expansion of the sewer system to include all of the SPA will mitigate the potential for on-site sewage disposal related contamination in the upland areas. The West Rutland Zoning Regulations have delineated the SPA as the Source Water Protection Overlay District. Zone 1 is defined as "…wherever possible, the area shall be free of potential sources of contamination." Within Zone 2 are prohibited many uses that are known sources of contamination. Zone 3 also has conditional land uses that may be approved if the landowner can meet the performance standards outlined for the District. A copy of the Zoning Regulations for the Source Water Protection Overlay District is available at the town hall. 117 | P a g e West Rutland Zoning Regulations (Adopted 2022) The West Rutland Planning and Zoning Boards should intensively consider the types of proposed developments, their associated PSOC's and their potential impacts to Wells 2 and 3 prior to approving any developments. Of great concern from a contaminant standpoint is the potential development of the existing active farm to the south of the wells, at the edge of Zone 2. Another great potential for future development is in the upland undeveloped properties to the west of Dewey Avenue in Zone 3. III. M ANAGEMENT PLAN Based on the nature of the contaminant threats, the locations of PSOC's and the geology and hydrogeology of the unconfined groundwater aquifer serving Wells 2 and 3, there is a definite risk of contamination to these wells. There are a variety of strategies which can be implemented to protect/manage the SPA. Management strategies can be divided into two categories: regulatory and non- regulatory. Regulatory strategies involve ordinances aimed at controlling land-use. Non- regulatory approaches focus on voluntary action and community education. Depending on the level of current protection, the initial management plan should focus on non-regulatory actions such as public education. C ONTINGENCY PLAN The contingency pl an is developed to identify the location and provision of alternate drinking water supply(s) in the event of groundwater source contamination. Although no one can conceive of every type of water supply emergency which may develop, basic preparation can be made which will aid and expedite corrective actions during an emergency situation. Contingency planning should be reviewed and updated periodically to avoid wasting time during an emergency, trying to determine what to do. The Contingency Plan out lines the steps that the water system may take in the event that a water source well becomes contaminated, is at imminent risk of becoming contaminated (e.g. due to hazardous contaminant spill in the vicinity of the well) or declines in yield. The plan may also be implemented if there are mechanical problems with the water system which require repair, or there is contamination of a water storage tank. 120 | P a g e West Rutland Zoning Regulations (Adopted 2022) The above possible situations may result in a loss of water supply to the citizens of West Rutland for a number of hours, days, weeks or even permanently. The Contingency Plan specifies emergency response procedures including the names and phone numbers of key people/officials that may be needed to solve the particular problem. Water system officials will need to identify the appropriate people to call for each situation. In addition, short-term and long-term water supply alternatives are outlines.

Letter to Landowners West Rutland Water Department 35 Marble Street West Rutland, Vermont 05777 September 9, 2020 Dear Landowner, As required by the State of Vermont, West Rutland Water System has been working to develop a Source Protection Plan to protect our drinking water wells. West Rutland Water System is being assisted by Vermont Rural Water Association to update this plan. The purpose of the plan is to identify potential contaminants and to manage and maintain the quality and quantity of our public drinking water sources. Your land is located within the source protection area (see enclosed map). If you own a home in the source protection area, you may have already been contacted to provide information necessary in the development of this plan. A source protection area is the land from which contaminants are considered likely to reach a well. Within a source protection area, human land uses and naturally occurring materials may cause a public water system to become vulnerable to contamination. While naturally-occurring contaminants can usually be 132 | P a g e West Rutland Zoning Regulations (Adopted 2022) controlled by treatment methods, property owners are often able to manage their land uses to further lower the risk of contamination. Land use activities that occur within a Source Protection Area have the ability to negatively impact a water source. For example, activities such as improperly disposing of household hazardous wastes and motor oil, septic system failures, and spillage of gasoline or home heating fuel all have the potential to contaminate a water source. Many of the negative impacts associated with these activities can be avoided with good management. If you have any questions, please contact the West Rutland Water System at (802) 438-5633. Copies of our Source Protection Plan will be available for review at the West Rutland Town Clerk's Office and the State of Vermont DEC - Drinking Water and Groundwater Protection Division in Montpelier. Thank you in advance for helping us protect the drinking water in our community. Sincerely, Seth Pietryka West Rutland Water System 133 | P a g e West Rutland Zoning Regulations (Adopted 2022) ATTACHMENT D
